notices.QC: **REGULATORY NOTICE — Loi 25 (QC):** Severe penalties apply. Penal fines can reach **$25M or 4% of worldwide turnover** (whichever is greater). The CAI and affected individuals must be notified promptly where there is a risk of serious injury.
notices.ON: **REGULATORY NOTICE — PIPEDA + PHIPA (ON):** If PHI is involved, PHIPA applies: administrative penalties up to **$500,000** and offence fines up to **$1,000,000** for organizations. Class-action risk is the primary financial driver in Ontario.
notices.AB: **REGULATORY NOTICE — PIPA (AB):** Notification required when there is a real risk of significant harm. Fines are statutory but low; focus is on cause remediation.
notices.BC: **REGULATORY NOTICE — PIPA (BC):** Similar to Alberta. Recent case law strengthens “Intrusion upon Seclusion” tort claims.
notices.OTHER: **REGULATORY NOTICE — PIPEDA (Federal):** Mandatory breach reporting to the OPC when there is a Real Risk of Significant Harm (RROSH). Non-compliance is a serious offence.
notices.FED: **REGULATORY NOTICE — PIPEDA (Federal):** Mandatory breach reporting to the OPC when there is a Real Risk of Significant Harm (RROSH). Non-compliance is a serious offence.
notices.FIN: **REGULATORY NOTICE — PIPEDA + OSFI B-13:** Federally regulated financial entities must comply with OSFI B-13. Failures trigger supervisory intervention and increased capital requirements.

ncta.title: NCTA 2025–2026 STRATEGIC INTELLIGENCE
ncta.intro: Intelligence from the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (CCCS) highlights an aggressive threat landscape targeting critical infrastructure and data extortion.

trends.label: AI-Enabled Threats
trends.body: Adversaries are using LLMs to craft convincing spear-phishing lures and automate vulnerability scanning at scale.

trends.label: Living off the Land (LotL)
trends.body: Threat actors (Volt Typhoon, etc.) use legitimate admin tools to remain undetected inside Canadian networks for months.

trends.label: Ransomware Evolution
trends.body: Shift from encryption to pure data extortion. Attackers pressure victims by directly contacting clients and regulators.

trends.label: Supply Chain Risk
trends.body: Reliance on managed service providers (MSPs) and cloud platforms remains a critical single-point-of-failure vector.

trends.label: Disruptive Activism
trends.body: Geopolitical tensions are escalating DDoS and defacement campaigns against Canadian public and critical institutions.

ncta.alert: **Ransomware:** The average ransom paid by Canadian organizations reached **CA$1.13M** in 2023 and continues rising. IBM 2025 puts the national average breach cost at **CA$6.98M**. Finance (CA$9.97M) and Industrial (CA$8.39M) sectors face the steepest exposure.

disclaimer: This simulator produces illustrative estimates based on Canadian industry averages, published breach cost research, and legal precedent. Figures are probabilistic ranges presented as point estimates for clarity. This tool does not constitute legal, actuarial, or financial advice. Consult qualified counsel before making risk management or insurance decisions.

assumptions.title: Model assumptions & sources
assumptions.intro: Every figure the simulator uses comes from data/model.json. Values tagged “Author estimate” do not have an external citation yet.
rules: Technical effort = incident IR hours × revenue effort multiplier (Large is capped at 70%), then split into IR, forensics and IT recovery using the effort ratios and root-cause multipliers.

Notification, credit monitoring, regulatory fines and the class-action reserve only apply when personal information is exposed: always for data breaches and insider incidents, for ransomware only when exfiltration occurred, for BEC only when mailbox personal information was accessed, never for DDoS.
Regulatory fines and settlements are expected values: fine or settlement amount × probability.
Ransomware assumes the ransom is paid; BEC includes the fraudulent transfer loss.

Insurance: the deductible sits inside the coverage limit, so the insurer pays at most limit − deductible. The 3-year premium increase only applies when a claim is paid. Net = gross − covered + premium increase.

Timeline: Year 1 holds response, counsel, notification, monitoring, business impact and the premium increase; fines and settlements land in Year 2+. Variable X is projected as revenue × Variable X rate per year for years 3–5.
